name: IBM Quantum
short_summary: IBM Quantum (est. 2016, Yorktown Heights NY) is IBM's quantum computing division operating the world's first public cloud quantum service (IBM Quantum Experience, 2016) and the largest fleet of superconducting processors. Its hardware roadmap progressed from 127-qubit Eagle (2021) through 433-qubit Osprey (2022) to 1,121-qubit Condor and 133-qubit Heron (2023), with Heron powering the modular IBM Quantum System Two. The division also publishes Qiskit, the most widely used open-source quantum SDK. IBM targets 200-qubit / 100 M-gate Starling by 2029 and a 2,000-qubit / 1 B-gate Blue Jay system by 2033.

Demonstrated evidence for quantum utility on a 127-qubit Eagle processor in Nature (June 2023), executing circuits beyond the reach of brute-force classical simulation
IBM Quantum System Two (Yorktown Heights, 2023) is the industry's first modular quantum computer, housing three Heron processors with a shared cryogenic infrastructure
Publicly committed roadmap to quantum-centric supercomputing extending to 2033 (Starling 200-qubit / 100 M gates by 2029; Blue Jay 2,000-qubit / 1 B gates by 2033)

milestones.claim: IBM launched IBM Quantum Experience — the first cloud-based service giving the public hands-on access to a real quantum processor (5 superconducting qubits) hosted at the T.J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights.

Released Qiskit (Quantum Information Software Kit) as an open-source Python SDK, the first publicly available quantum software development kit, enabling users to build and run quantum circuits on IBM hardware and simulators.

Launched the IBM Q Network — an ecosystem of Fortune 500 companies, academic institutions, and national labs (initial 12 members including JPMorgan Chase, Daimler, Samsung, Barclays, Oak Ridge National Lab, University of Oxford) with early commercial access to IBM Q systems.

Unveiled IBM Q System One at CES 2019 — the world's first integrated commercial quantum computing system, housing a 20-qubit processor in a 9-foot borosilicate glass enclosure designed for continuous operation outside a research lab.

name: IonQ
short_summary: IonQ (founded 2015, College Park MD) is the first publicly traded pure-play quantum computing company (NYSE IONQ), building general-purpose gate-based trapped-ion quantum computers spun out of work by Christopher Monroe and Jungsang Kim at the University of Maryland and Duke. Its systems — Harmony, Aria, Forte and Tempo — report performance in Algorithmic Qubits (#AQ), feature all-to-all connectivity and near-room-temperature operation, and are available across AWS, Azure and Google Cloud. In 2025 IonQ reported a world-record 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity and rapidly expanded through acquisitions including Oxford Ionics ($1.075B), ID Quantique, Qubitekk and Lightsynq, building an integrated quantum-computing and quantum-networking business.

Reports performance in "Algorithmic Qubits" (#AQ), an application-oriented benchmark, rather than raw physical-qubit count
Systems operate at or near room temperature (no dilution refrigerator), and are available via all three major clouds — AWS Braket, Azure Quantum and Google Cloud
Aggressive vertical integration through acquisitions spanning quantum networking (Qubitekk, ID Quantique), photonic interconnects (Lightsynq) and chip-scale ion-trap control (Oxford Ionics)

short_summary: Google Quantum AI (founded 2012, Santa Barbara CA) is Alphabet's superconducting quantum computing division. It achieved quantum supremacy with the 53-qubit Sycamore processor in 2019, demonstrated below-threshold quantum error correction with the 105-qubit Willow chip in December 2024, and claimed verifiable quantum advantage with the Quantum Echoes algorithm in October 2025. The division operates its own qubit fabrication facility and publishes the open-source Cirq framework, pursuing a five-milestone roadmap toward commercially useful error-corrected quantum computation by 2029.

name: Element Six
short_summary: Element Six (founded 1946, Didcot, UK) is a De Beers Group company and the world's leading manufacturer of synthetic diamond and superhard materials, with over 1,900 employees across the UK, Ireland, Germany, South Africa, and the US. It is the primary global supplier of quantum-grade CVD single-crystal diamond for NV-center qubit research, selling the DNV-B1 and DNV-B14 product lines that provide engineered NV-centre density for quantum sensing, quantum computing, quantum networking, and room-temperature masers. Key quantum partnerships include IonQ (foundry-compatible diamond films for quantum memories and photonic interconnects, announced September 2025), AWS (quantum networking research collaboration), the University of Maryland Quantum Technology Center / Walsworth Group (magnetometry characterisation), and Orbray (wafer-scale 50 mm diamond substrates). Element Six was selected for the DARPA LADDIS and UWBGS defence programs (2023-2024) and made a strategic investment in quantum interconnect startup Lightsynq (acquired by IonQ in June 2025). The company's Global Innovation Centre is located at Harwell, Didcot, Oxfordshire, and its advanced US manufacturing facility is in Gresham, Oregon.

name: Pasqal
short_summary: Pasqal (founded 2019, Massy, France) builds neutral-atom quantum computers using arrays of rubidium atoms held in optical tweezers and entangled through Rydberg interactions, supporting both analog quantum simulation and digital gate-based computing. An Institut d'Optique spin-out, its founders include Georges-Olivier Reymond, Christophe Jurczak, 2022 Nobel laureate Alain Aspect, Antoine Browaeys and Thierry Lahaye. Its €100M (~$108M) Series B, led by Temasek in January 2023, funds a path toward 1,000-qubit machines and fault-tolerant architectures.

differentiators: Neutral-atom quantum processors using arrays of rubidium atoms held in optical tweezers and entangled via Rydberg interactions, supporting both analog quantum simulation and digital gate-based computing
Spun out of Institut d'Optique research by Antoine Browaeys and Thierry Lahaye, with 2022 Nobel laureate Alain Aspect among the founders
Atom arrays are reconfigurable and operate near room temperature (no dilution refrigerator), enabling relatively compact, lower-power systems
Pursuing a clear scaling path toward 1,000-qubit machines and, longer term, fault-tolerant neutral-atom architectures

name: Quantum Diamonds
short_summary: Quantum Diamonds (founded 2022, Munich) builds diamond NV-centre quantum-sensing systems that non-destructively image magnetic fields to localise defects in advanced semiconductor chips. Founded by Kevin Berghoff and Fleming Bruckmaier, it has raised early venture funding and is building a EUR 150M+ chip-inspection facility in Munich backed by the German and Bavarian governments under the European Chips Act.

differentiators: Diamond NV quantum sensors image magnetic fields from electrical currents to localise defects in buried, 2.5D/3D chip structures non-destructively
Operates from room temperature to cryogenic and high temperatures, with high-throughput wide-field imaging
Targets the semiconductor industry (R&D, failure analysis, process optimisation) rather than only research
Spun out of TU Munich / LMU with EXIST founder support
approach.elevator_pitch: Quantum Diamonds uses nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond to image the magnetic fields from currents inside chips, enabling non-destructive, micrometer-scale failure analysis of advanced semiconductors.

products.description: Diamond NV-centre magnetic-imaging system for non-destructive localisation of defects in advanced semiconductor chips and packages.
products.name: NV quantum-sensing chip-inspection system

rounds.notes: ~$7.7M raised from investors incl. the EIC Accelerator, IQ Capital, Earlybird and First Momentum.

milestones.claim: Founded in Munich by Kevin Berghoff and Fleming Bruckmaier, supported by the EXIST Founder's Grant, from quantum-sensor research at TU Munich.
Announced a EUR 150M+ quantum chip-inspection facility in Munich, backed by the German federal and Bavarian governments under the European Chips Act.

name: JoS QUANTUM
short_summary: JoS QUANTUM (founded 2018, Frankfurt) develops quantum and quantum-inspired algorithms for the financial, insurance and energy industries, focused on risk analysis, simulation and optimisation.
